readme: Reviewed near-duplicate commodity pairs for audit-commodity-dupes.ps1. An entry asserts a human checked BOTH ids and they are genuinely DIFFERENT PURCHASES, with the reason written down. NEVER add an entry to silence a finding - a real duplicate is merged (rebid the consumers, drop the loser row; see the 2026-08-15 bread-crumbs/breadcrumbs merge), not allowlisted. Pairs declared in recipe-floor-id-map.json are honored automatically and do NOT belong here (two copies of one ruling drift).

allow.reviewed_by: claude, confirmed against both board rows
allow.reason: Different vegetables, not a spelling drift. Broccolini is a broccoli/gai-lan hybrid sold in bunches at a different price point; the suffix rule fires on the shared stem only.
Honey is a sweetener, honeydew is a melon. The suffix rule fires on the shared stem only; the two never price the same food.
Whole coconut (produce, per each) versus coconut oil (pantry fat, per fl oz). Different foods, different aisles, different units.
